- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 3–5% upward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is trending upward.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.30), model often fails to anticipate sustained rally; extend upward bias for 3–5 days beyond the sentiment peak.  
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in low-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days.
